chapter: Arranging for other bandleaders and closing talk
title: Fletcher's band reads 'Christopher Columbus' on a break and it becomes the theme
summary: Horace showed Fletcher the tune and the band read it downstairs during intermission; it opened the next set, broke up the Roseland and became Fletcher's theme.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Okay, I think we're back on the air now. We were talking about Claude Hopkins, and you had told me about the Christopher Columbus and that his band played it before Fletcher's did even. That was just a read through, right?
Did you later give him a copy of the arrangement or --

I didn't get back to him, because (Unintelligible). After I traveled from Harlem down to 51st and Broadway, Fletcher was just going on one of his break, and I had heard the thing and heard how it sounds, you know, and I was real enthused about it, you know, because I wanted to see what the reaction would be from Chu, you know, Berry, the saxophonist that used to play this riff that the tune was written around, you know.
And I told Fletcher about it, and I said, "Hey, Smack" -- I called him Smack, you know -- "Hey, I've got a tune here, I think, that might be all right." I hummed a little

bit of it to him, and I said, -- 'I took it off of a riff that Chu plays all the time,' we're going very shortly. He says, 'Well, if you want to take a break why don't it we run it over very quick. we'll go downstairs and (unintelligible). So he told the guys to bring all their horns downstairs (unintelligible). at the intermission. read excellent in those days. So we Everybody naturally, (unintelligible), took it downstairs, and I passed it out, I had all the parts for the guys. (Unintelligible). Fletcher said, 'What's the tempo on this thing?' So (unintelligible). I kinda snapped my fingers and gave the beat with my feet. So he stomped it off -- I did, rather, I think I (Inaudible portion). did the stomping off.

They started out, man, playing, and it was swinging, and they got to the solos, and everybody in the band liked it. They went back upstairs, it was the first number they opened up with. Man, you should have seen the expressions on the dance people's faces when this thing was up, because they were real hip there. the people at the Roseland, they could dance, you know, and, man, it broke the house up.
And I felt so good, you know, and, oh, Chu stuck his big stomach out, you know, one of those things. There it was, and the thing turned out to be the theme song of Fletcher, you know.
And he was broadcasting in those days, from we went on tours. I'm ahead of myself, That's usual there, and tours (unintelligible). "Christopher Columbus became quite a part of it.
